# Implementation Plan: Migrate fork flags onto codex experimental features

<!-- ralph-meta {"overviewTaskId":"codex-fork-flags-to-experimental-features-migration"} -->

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-12. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/codex-fork-flags-to-experimental-features-migration/plan.md`.*

## Overview

This plan migrates the codex fork's remaining ad-hoc runtime toggles onto the canonical feature
registry while preserving the fork's conflict-minimization discipline. The work has three active
product surfaces: (1) make `Feature::AnthropicModels` the sole source of truth for Anthropic /
Claude-via-Copilot support, eliminating the launcher-local `enable_anthropic` control path that
causes the persistence bug, including the persisted-Claude model reselection path in `tui/src/app.rs`;
(2) move the paste-burst heuristic off the top-level `disable_paste_burst` bool and into a
default-off `features.legacy_paste_burst_heuristic` entry that represents the legacy opt-in path;
and (3) move `style_user_messages` from launcher-env mediation into a default-off
`features.user_message_styling` entry. Both legacy inputs remain only as one-release compatibility
adapters that map into the canonical feature path rather than owning runtime behavior. Existing
proper features (`managed_hooks`, `background_process_notification`, `mcp_server_notifications`)
remain structurally unchanged, and Knob A / Knob B stay out of scope.

The guiding design is to keep runtime authority in `features/src/lib.rs` plus resolved
`config.features.enabled(Feature::X)` checks, and to demote older launcher / config knobs to either
compatibility adapters or removal points. That satisfies the fork rule that new divergent behavior
must use the experimental-features mechanism, and it reduces future rebase risk by limiting
upstream-canonical changes to feature declarations, config-resolution collapse points, a few TUI
call sites, and the required SANDBOX PATCH bookkeeping in `docs/implementation/patch-surface.md`.

## Research Findings
### Codebase Context

- Canonical feature registration lives in
  `codex/external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/features/src/lib.rs`, where `Stage`, `Feature`,
  `FeatureSpec`, and `FEATURES` define lifecycle, key names, and `default_enabled` values.
- The existing Anthropic and managed-hooks fork features already show the intended pattern:
  `Feature::AnthropicModels` / `Feature::ManagedHooks` are registered in `features/src/lib.rs` and
  their effective values are resolved in `core/src/config/mod.rs`.
- Launcher-owned config still carries the two ad-hoc surfaces this task needs to retire:
  `style_user_messages` and `enable_anthropic` in
  `codex/codex-rs-overlay/codex-copilot-launcher/src/config.rs`, with runtime env mediation in
  `src/main.rs`.
- The paste-burst toggle is still a top-level config bool in
  `codex/external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/config/src/config_toml.rs`, resolved into
  `Config.disable_paste_burst` in `core/src/config/mod.rs`, and consumed by TUI composer wiring in
  `tui/src/chatwidget/constructor.rs` and `tui/src/public_widgets/composer_input.rs`.
- User-message styling currently reads `CODEX_TUI_USER_MESSAGE_STYLE` once per process in

  configuration path.
- Codex research found an additional Anthropic persistence seam in `tui/src/app.rs`: the app can
  overwrite the gate-safe `bootstrap.default_model` with persisted `config.model`, so the migration
  must also handle invalid persisted Claude defaults when the gate is off.

### Technical Constraints

- Every new migrated behavior must live behind a canonical `features.<name>` key with
  `default_enabled = false`, matching the operator's fork convention and the feature registry's
  intended role.
- Upstream-canonical edits must carry `// SANDBOX PATCH:` markers and matching `patch-surface.md`
  invariant / replant updates in the same change.
- The plan worktree was created without submodule initialization, so codex-source verification was
  performed from the primary checkout. The actual implementation should still happen in the codex
  submodule worktree created by the impl phase.
- The checked-out source currently resolves `disable_paste_burst` with `unwrap_or(false)`, even
  though some fork docs still describe a default-true path. The implementation should treat the
  current source plus the migration intent as authoritative and update the bookkeeping accordingly.
- The paste-burst migration must coordinate with `codex-paste-guard-perf-and-dropped-text`, whose
  intended end state is "heuristic off by default; legacy heuristic available only as opt-in."
- The TUI bottom-pane guidance requires `paste_burst.rs` / `chat_composer.rs` docs to stay aligned
  with any state-machine behavior changes.
- If `ConfigToml` or nested config types change, the implementation must run
  `just write-config-schema`.

## Approach
### Architecture

1. **Anthropic: remove duplicate launcher/runtime authority and keep the existing feature bit.**
   `Feature::AnthropicModels` is already the correct runtime switch. The migration should remove
   launcher-direct `CODEX_ENABLE_ANTHROPIC` ownership **and** remove the runtime env fallback from
   `model-provider/src/anthropic_gate.rs`, so `features.anthropic_models` is the only durable
   runtime authority. If launcher compatibility is retained for one release, `enable_anthropic`
   should translate into `-c features.anthropic_models=<bool>` before config resolution rather than
   mutating env. The acceptance criteria must explicitly cover the persistence bug where Anthropic
   remains enabled without the launcher flag.

2. **Paste burst: introduce a default-off experimental feature for the legacy heuristic path.**
   The runtime should stop treating `disable_paste_burst` as the primary toggle. Instead, feature
   resolution should own the behavior via `features.legacy_paste_burst_heuristic`
   (`Stage::Experimental`, `default_enabled = false`). The older top-level `disable_paste_burst`
   input should be treated as a one-release deprecated compatibility adapter during migration, and
   the resolved config semantics should invert from the feature-backed value
   (`Config.disable_paste_burst = !features.enabled(...)`) so existing TUI consumers keep their
   current meaning while the canonical source becomes positive-form.

3. **User-message styling: replace env mediation with a default-off experimental feature-backed TUI gate.**
   The launcher should no longer own the runtime gate via `CODEX_TUI_USER_MESSAGE_STYLE`.
   `tui/src/style.rs` should instead read `features.user_message_styling`
   (`Stage::Experimental`, `default_enabled = false`), with the launcher keeping only a one-release
   compatibility adapter from `style_user_messages` into the canonical feature path so upstream
   styling remains the baseline unless explicitly enabled. To avoid threading `Config` through every
   style callsite, the implementation should add a small one-time TUI install seam (for example, a
   style-gate installer in `tui/src/style.rs` called from `tui/src/chatwidget/constructor.rs` or
   equivalent bootstrap code) so existing shared style helpers can keep their current signatures.

4. **Bookkeeping: update the divergence ledger with every upstream seam.**
   The plan must include the corresponding `patch-surface.md` rows, invariant updates, and replant
   notes so future upstream rebases can mechanically recover the migrated feature seams.

### Chosen Seams / Conflict Budget

| Surface | Chosen seam | Why this seam | Edit budget | Re-conflict probability |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| Anthropic cleanup | Existing upstream-canonical feature/config/model-provider seams plus launcher compatibility translation | `Feature::AnthropicModels` already exists, so the minimal correct change is to remove parallel launcher/env authority rather than invent a new overlay gate. | ~5 files + tests/docs | Medium |
| Paste-burst migration | New feature rows + config-resolution collapse + existing TUI callsites/docs | The runtime behavior already exists in TUI; adding a new overlay abstraction would increase surface area without reducing upstream conflict. | ~6-8 files + tests/docs | Medium |
| Styling migration | New feature rows + one-time TUI style-gate install seam + existing styling helpers | A one-time install seam preserves current helper signatures across many render callsites and avoids large-scale plumbing through TUI rendering code. | ~6-8 files + tests/snapshots/docs | Medium-High |
| Patch-surface closeout | Existing `patch-surface.md` / `codex/CLAUDE.md` guidance files | Required by repo policy; keeping the replant notes beside the touched seams reduces future rebase ambiguity. | 2 docs + invariant/test mapping | Medium |

### Implementation Strategy

1. **Registry and compatibility design pass.**
   Add `legacy_paste_burst_heuristic` and `user_message_styling` as `Stage::Experimental`,
   `default_enabled = false` feature entries, keep `Feature::AnthropicModels` unchanged, and
   document the one-release compatibility adapters / conflict-minimizing seams in the patch
   registry.
2. **Anthropic single-source cleanup.**
   Remove launcher-local direct Anthropic mediation, update `model-provider/src/anthropic_gate.rs`
   so runtime no longer accepts `CODEX_ENABLE_ANTHROPIC` as a parallel authority, preserve
   `Feature::AnthropicModels` as the sole resolved runtime gate, and add regression coverage for the
   persistence bug, including the persisted-model fallback path in `tui/src/app.rs`.
3. **Paste-burst feature migration.**
   Introduce the new default-off feature, collapse legacy `disable_paste_burst` input into the
   canonical feature if needed for compatibility, update composer wiring, and keep state-machine
   docs in sync.
4. **User-message styling feature migration.**
   Add the new default-off feature, replace the env-based style gate with resolved feature access,
   and update any launcher compatibility or migration handling.
5. **Patch-surface and verification closeout.**
   Refresh `patch-surface.md`, any related config schema output, and targeted tests / snapshots for
   launcher, core config, and TUI behavior.

## Scope
### In Scope

- Removing launcher-local Anthropic runtime authority and consolidating on `Feature::AnthropicModels`
  as the single source of truth.
- Covering the Anthropic persistence bug in the plan's acceptance criteria and verification surface.
- Adding default-off feature-registry entries for paste-burst legacy opt-in behavior and
  user-message styling.
- Migrating runtime consumers of `disable_paste_burst` and `style_user_messages` onto canonical
  feature-backed configuration.
- Updating SANDBOX PATCH markers, patch-surface invariants, replant notes, and config-schema output
  when required.

### Out of Scope

- Structural changes to `managed_hooks`, `background_process_notification`, or
  `mcp_server_notifications`.
- Knob A default reasoning policy or Knob B context-tier selection.
- A release cut, build-pipeline changes, or upstream contribution work.
- Any redesign of the paste-burst state machine beyond what is necessary to move the toggle surface.

## Risk Areas

- **Anthropic compatibility migration:** removing launcher-local authority without breaking intended
  opt-in workflows needs a clear compatibility policy and tests for both feature and legacy entry
  points, plus persisted-model fallback handling so hidden Claude defaults do not reappear.
- **Paste-burst compatibility drift:** the deprecated `disable_paste_burst` alias must map cleanly
  onto `features.legacy_paste_burst_heuristic` for one release without reintroducing dual authority.
- **Default flip for styling:** `style_user_messages` currently behaves as default-on. The new
  feature mechanism requires `features.user_message_styling` default-off with only a temporary
  compatibility adapter, which is a deliberate user-visible behavior change and must be captured in
  tests / snapshots.
- **Patch-surface drift:** missing invariant rows or replant notes will make the next upstream rebase
  fragile.
- **Stale operator guidance:** `codex/CLAUDE.md` and `patch-surface.md` currently contain
  paste-burst-default guidance that conflicts with the new feature-backed direction; if not updated,
  future rebases will resurrect the old default.
- **Shared TUI wiring:** composer, public composer wrapper, and bottom-pane docs must stay aligned so
  the paste-burst migration does not leave stale documentation or mismatched defaults.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `Feature::AnthropicModels` remains the only runtime source of truth for Anthropic enablement; the
   launcher no longer independently controls Anthropic behavior via `enable_anthropic`.
2. The implementation explicitly covers the persistence bug: Anthropic cannot remain enabled merely
   because an older launcher-local setting or env mediation path diverged from the resolved feature.
3. `model-provider/src/anthropic_gate.rs` no longer treats `CODEX_ENABLE_ANTHROPIC` as a parallel
   runtime authority; any retained compatibility adapter translates into
   `features.anthropic_models` before config resolution rather than being re-read at runtime.
4. When Anthropic is disabled, a persisted Claude `config.model` no longer overrides the
   gate-filtered bootstrap default in `tui/src/app.rs`; the app clears or replaces the hidden Claude
   selection with an available safe model and does so with explicit regression coverage.
5. `features.legacy_paste_burst_heuristic` is added in `features/src/lib.rs` as
   `Stage::Experimental` with `default_enabled = false`, and it becomes the canonical runtime
   switch for the legacy paste-burst heuristic.
6. Any remaining `disable_paste_burst` config input is a one-release deprecated compatibility alias
   that maps into `features.legacy_paste_burst_heuristic`; runtime TUI wiring reads only the
   canonical feature-backed value, with resolved config semantics preserving existing call-site
   meaning, consistent with `codex-paste-guard-perf-and-dropped-text`.
7. `features.user_message_styling` is added in `features/src/lib.rs` as `Stage::Experimental` with
   `default_enabled = false`, and it becomes the canonical runtime switch for Claude-style user
   message / proposed-plan styling.
8. `style_user_messages` remains only as a one-release launcher compatibility adapter that maps into
   `features.user_message_styling`; runtime styling no longer depends on
   `CODEX_TUI_USER_MESSAGE_STYLE`.
9. The styling migration uses a concrete one-time install seam so the shared helpers in
   `tui/src/style.rs` can read the resolved feature-backed value without re-plumbing every rendering
   callsite individually.
10. If legacy launcher/config compatibility is retained for Anthropic, paste burst, or styling, it
   maps into the canonical feature path only and is documented as transitional rather than
   authoritative.
11. `managed_hooks`, `background_process_notification`, and `mcp_server_notifications` remain
   structurally unchanged aside from any necessary documentation refresh.
12. Knob A and Knob B remain untouched by the implementation.
13. Every upstream-canonical edit introduced by the migration carries `// SANDBOX PATCH:` markers and
   matching `docs/implementation/patch-surface.md` invariant / replant updates.
14. Patch-surface closeout includes the enforcing guard/test mapping for each new or changed
   invariant, and the plan / implementation notes retain the chosen seams, edit-budget estimate,
   and expected re-conflict surface for future rebases.
15. If config schema-bearing types change, `just write-config-schema` is run and the generated schema
   output is updated in the same change.
16. Targeted verification covers launcher, model-provider, core-config, and TUI surfaces (`just test -p` for
   touched crates, plus TUI snapshot review / acceptance for transcript, history-cell, proposed-plan,
   and streaming-plan surfaces when user-visible styling output changes).

## Suggested Decomposition

This work should run **serially as one impl member**. The stories all overlap on the same core
surfaces - `features/src/lib.rs`, `core/src/config/mod.rs`, launcher compatibility seams, TUI
call-site wiring, and `patch-surface.md` bookkeeping - so parallel implementation would create
merge-conflict churn without reducing risk.

- `execution_mode` rationale: All four stories depend on a single canonical feature-resolution model
